records.name: Friends of the Cresheim Trail
records.summary: A volunteer nonprofit that builds and looks after trails linking Wissahickon Valley Park with Fort Washington State Park. Its current project is a rail trail on old railroad land.
records.what_you_do: Join cleanups and trail workdays, help at fundraisers and booths, or support the group with a membership donation.

schedule.text: Volunteer workdays run through the year, most on weekends and some on weekday mornings. The group lists its dates on its 2026 workday page, and some dates are still to be announced.

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteer workdays. The group suggests a donation of about $50 to join its group.

requirements.gear: Tools and gloves are provided, and you may bring your own. Clothing and other items are not stated.

first_step.how: Check the Volunteer Workdays 2026 page for the next date, then email info@cresheimtrail.org to ask how to sign up.
first_step.basis: Workdays are open to volunteers of every skill level, and the group gives an email address to ask how to join. The page does not describe a sign-up step, so this is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: A workday is outdoor trail work, such as litter pickup, pulling invasive plants, planting trees and shrubs, clearing sightlines, and trail repairs, and the group says there is work for every skill level. Tools and gloves are provided, and you may bring your own. Some workdays start at 9 am, and dates can change.
first_visit_tips: Email info@cresheimtrail.org before a first workday to ask about sign up and the meeting spot, since not every date lists one.
Mermaid Park at 7645 Germantown Ave is the usual start point, but check each date because some list a different meeting place.
Tools and gloves are provided, so you do not need your own, though you may bring them.
Check the workday page for weather cancellations before you travel. The group calls off work only in severe weather.

records.notes: The group's own 2026 workday page and home page are current, so confidence is high. Changes from tier 1: schedule.text no longer names the May 2026 cleanup and fundraiser, which are one-time dated events; days now come from the 2026 workday page (Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday dates); season changed from spring to year_round because the page lists workdays in every month; commitment changed from drop_in to one_off because the page does not say workdays are drop in and each workday is a single outing; the fundraiser ticket price is removed from cost.text. The home page dates the Toast to the Trail fundraiser to May 29, 2026. Instagram posts that the site links to (sign-up through a link in bio, parking for the May 16 event) were not used for any fact.

records.name: Friends of the Rail Park
records.summary: A nonprofit building a three-mile greenway from old rail tracks, in three sections across ten neighborhoods from Northern Liberties to Fairmount Park. The park is free and open every day, and volunteers help with clean-ups and green-ups.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer clean-up or green-up, book a guided tour, or become a member.

schedule.text: The park is open every day from 7 am to 10 pm. Volunteers can join clean-ups held monthly, at the park and in the nearby community.

cost.text: The park is free to visit, and the self-guided audio tour of Phase One is free too. Guided tour prices and membership amounts are not listed on the site.

access.notes: The Noble Street entrance is step-free, with an ADA-compliant slope up to the far end of the park. The Callowhill Street entrance has stairs only, and the park has no restrooms. In-person tours are in English only.

requirements.gear: For tours, wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather. Water is recommended.

first_step.how: Sign up for a volunteer clean-up through GivePulse, or book a public tour with the Book Now button on the Book a Tour page.
first_step.basis: Volunteers join monthly clean-ups through GivePulse, and public tours are posted with dates and a Book Now button. Experience and age rules for clean-ups are not stated.
first_step.what_to_expect: Clean-ups are volunteer work at the park and in the nearby community, held monthly. The site does not say how long they run, what time they start, or what to wear, so ask before you come. Tours are outdoors with a fair amount of walking, so plan for the weather and wear comfortable shoes.
first_visit_tips: Use the Noble Street entrance, which is step-free. The Callowhill Street side is stairs only.
Use a restroom before you arrive, since the park has none.
For tours, bring water and wear comfortable shoes, because the tour is entirely outdoors.
Public tours start at 2700 Pennsylvania Ave and end near 12th and Callowhill. Buses 49, 32, 7, 43 and 48 run nearby, and the Broad Street Subway is about 5 minutes on foot from the end point.

records.notes: Changes from tier 1: the October events moved out of schedule.text and what_you_do (they are dated, so they live in last_sign_of_life). The Wednesday and Saturday days came only from those one-time October events, so they are removed; recurring is now true for the monthly clean-ups the FAQ describes. Conflict to resolve: the FAQ says Pennsylvania and Delaware residents with a qualifying ACCESS or EBT card can book free tours, but the Book a Tour page does not mention ACCESS or EBT discounts, so the free-tour claim is left out. kids_ok is true because the FAQ says children and strollers are permitted on tours; park rules for kids are not stated. Membership fees are not stated. The 'ten neighborhoods' detail in the summary was not on the pages read and is carried from tier 1.

records.name: Friends of the Wissahickon
records.summary: Volunteers who look after the trails, streams and woods of Wissahickon Valley Park. They hold public service days to clear drains, fix trails, pull invasive plants and pick up litter.
records.what_you_do: Join a registered service day to work on trails, plant, pull invasive vines and pick up trash. Trained volunteer corps take on longer roles such as trail ambassadors and crew leaders.

schedule.text: Weekly crews work on Wednesday and Sunday mornings. Other service days, including Thursday and Saturday events from 9 am to noon, are posted on the Volunteer Service Days page, and registration is required for each one.

cost.text: The group's pages list no fee to volunteer and no membership amounts.

access.notes: Most trails are not wheelchair accessible, and the group suggests Forbidden Drive as an alternative. Valley Green Inn has disabled parking and a drop-off area at its ramps.

requirements.gear: Work gloves, sturdy closed shoes, long pants, sun protection, and a reusable water bottle are recommended. The page does not say whether tools are provided.

first_step.how: Pick a service day on the Volunteer Service Days page and click its date to register. The meeting place and details arrive by email before the day.
first_step.basis: Open to the public, with a clear way in: register for any listed service day on the site. The pages read do not say whether beginners are welcome, so this is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: A service day is a morning of hands-on park work, such as trash pickup, removing invasive plants, planting, graffiti removal, and trail fixes, and the tasks change from week to week. The group describes service days as fun and educational, and a chance to meet other park stewards. Listed Thursday and Saturday events run 9 am to noon, and weather cancellations are posted by 8 am.
first_visit_tips: Wear long pants, closed sturdy shoes (no open-toed shoes), and clothes you do not mind getting dirty.
Bring work gloves, sun protection such as a hat and sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle.
Check for a weather cancellation by 8 am on the day. Events are called off for heavy rain or snow, thunder and lightning, or high winds.
Teens 14 to 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the service day waiver form. Children under 14 must come with an adult.

records.notes: Changes from tier 1: schedule.text no longer names the October 8 and October 10, 2026 listings, which are one-off dated items. The deep pages show weekly Wednesday and Sunday crews and listed Thursday and Saturday events, and they mention Tuesday events in the email timing, so days now include those. newcomer_friendliness is lowered from 4 to 3: tier 1 said the group calls its service days the best place to start, but the volunteer pages and FAQ I read do not say that and do not say beginners are welcome. kids_ok is confirmed true (teens 14 to 18 with a waiver, children under 14 with an adult). Volunteer questions go to Marisa Miller at miller@fow.org per the volunteer page; the contact name Sarah Stevenson is carried from City data and is not on the pages read. The office address (40 West Evergreen Avenue, Suite 108) is the office, not a meeting point. The visit page had no hours, transit or visitor rules, so it is not cited. Some Oct 2026 dates on the news and events lists show no year in the listing, so none are used as a schedule fact.
